page.overview:
What is Dimension?

The concept of different dimensions is present throughout the writings of H. P. Lovecraft and the cosmic horror genre as a whole. The term is often used to describe universes or planes of existence different from our own, usually very alien in nature or following different laws and having different matter than our own universe. For example Cthulhu is from a different universe/dimension as he is described as being made of a different type of matter, as well as the Mi-Go. The Dreamlands are a famous example as well.

Dimensions can also be interpreted as higher spatial dimensions, which as seen in "Through the Gates of the Silver Key", go up until "archetypal infinity". Gates are a series of highly transcendental planes of existence which themselves surpass the very concept of higher dimensions. An unknown amount of gates exist, but there is stated to be a "multitude". The Ultimate Gate transcends all dimensions, universes and planes of existence and is where the Court of Azathoth is located in the "Ultimate Void", where the Outer Gods reside.

Fictional dimensions are often treated as places similar to "parallel worlds" or pocket dimensions, small and finite bounded other worlds. However sometimes the term is used less accurately or more poetically in Mythos works. For example the entities in "From Beyond" are visible when an attunement takes place. This attunement is treated as accessing a different dimension by most authors using it in their own pastiches. However, the original story deals with vibrations or frequencies so in that sense treating different frequencies as different dimensions is not correct. This is why some later writers deliberately obscure the intended nature of the "other dimensions" by using poetical or literary terms such as "realm" or "world" rather than "dimension". Dimension is the most scientific sounding of the common terms and in later Lovecraft, for example "The Dreams in the Witch-House", when magic-as-unknown-science has more or less replaced the supernatural, the term "dimension" is used in its applicable meaning from physics. Category:Dimensions Category:Locations Incorporated From Folklore, Myth & Religion
